verdicts.quote: Automatic promotion: when a seat opens, the head of the waitlist is booked at once. There is no offer, confirm or hold window.
FIFO by server-recorded join order. No priority tiers.
A member holding a time-overlapping booking elsewhere is handled by the existing eligibility rules (P-1). No new overlap rule.
verdicts.missing: Whether promotion into one class removes or otherwise resolves the member's entry on an overlapping class's waitlist; this depends on unknown existing rules (P-1).

verdicts.quote: whether a cancellation shortly after promotion is penalised. | A-1 and A-12: charge and penalise exactly as for a direct booking.
When a member's booking on a bookable class is cancelled and the waitlist is non-empty, the same operation runs a promotion pass.
PROMOTED (booking confirmed, with class and time)... Delivery failure of a notification does not undo a promotion, removal or expiry.
M1 and M2 cancel concurrently → promotions are M3 then M4 in either order, final booked [M3, M4], list []. ... two seats freed together serve two entries without duplication.
I-3 a member has at most one entry and is never both booked and waitlisted on the same class; ... Concurrent operations on one class behave as if they ran one at a time
it must be decided whether a promoted booking charges at promotion ... Default in force: charge and penalise exactly as for a direct booking.
verdicts.missing: What happens when payment for a promoted booking fails (removal, retry, seat passed on); whether charging occurs at all is unknown (P-1).

verdicts.quote: No cap on waitlist length. The rule is one entry per member per class. ... A cap would turn people away
The waitlist is open exactly while direct booking would be open (A-4). When the window closes, all entries expire and no promotion occurs, even if a seat is freed afterwards.
a capacity increase ... runs the same promotion pass ... Reducing capacity below the booked count removes no booking and promotes nobody until booked < capacity.
If staff cancel the class, all entries are removed and no booking is created.
Position = 1 + the number of entries ahead. ... new waitlist entry (class, member, join order)
No history is retained once an entry ends. The only durable trace is the "from waitlist" origin marker on the resulting booking.
A member can join, leave and view only their own entry. No response to a member contains another member's identity or position.
Staff get no waitlist view and no manual promotion in this change.
Roll-back: removing the feature leaves bookings intact; promoted bookings stay valid.
verdicts.missing: Whether there is an off switch, and whether the waitlist can be enabled per class or class type.

verdicts.quote: promotion happens inside the cancellation operation. When the cancel request has returned, a read-back already shows M3 booked, with no polling or delay.
Classes with open seats book exactly as before. ... Cancellation, the class listing and existing notifications for non-waitlist events are unchanged.
No existing data is migrated. Existing classes start with empty waitlists.
